 Eric Chelle Admits Late Arrivals Of Super Eagles’ Players Affected His Game Plan For Friday’s Clash With Tanzania
 By Sam O'Femi Fasetire - November 13, 2026 
 Facebook Twitter Pinterest WhatsApp 
 Super Eagles’ coach, Eric Sekou Chelle has admitted that the late arrivals by many of his players to the Nigerian team’s camp affected his plans for Friday’s Africa Cup of Nations qualifier versus Tanzania.
 Sports247 reports that, while Tanzania landed in Uyo with their full squad four days before the game at Godswill Akpabio International Stadium, their hosts did not have a full assemblage of invited players until late Wednesday.
 The development meant the Eagles had only two full training sessions – Thursday morning and evening – much to the chagrin of Chelle, who openly voiced his reservations during the pre-match press conference.
 The Franco-Malian tactician used the opportunity to express concern over the situation that left him and his crew with limited time to prepare, while also having to rush their process of dishing out tactical ideas to the players.
 “It’s difficult, but it’s my job. I just have find the best training structure and the best way to pass my idea of the game. Instead of four to three training sessions, you have only two,” said Chelle, who was celebrated on his birthday by the journalists present.
